*I’d hold shipping for one high-priority bug.*

*P1 — Renewal dates are clamped against the wrong month* — `src/schedule.js:6–7`
The code uses the number of days in the *source* month, then constructs a date in the *following* month. This both skips renewal months and fails to restore the original anchor after a short month:

• Jan 31, 2026, anchor 31 → *Mar 3*, expected *Feb 28*.
• Jan 31, 2028, anchor 31 → *Mar 2*, expected *Feb 29*.
• Feb 28, 2026, anchor 31 → *Mar 28*, expected *Mar 31*.
• Apr 30, 2026, anchor 31 → *May 30*, expected *May 31*.

Clamp against the *target month’s* length, while retaining the supplied anchor. Add regression tests for short-month transitions, leap February, and returning to the original anchor afterward.

*Validation:* All 5 existing tests pass, but an independent 2024–2028 month/anchor sweep found 66 incorrect results across 1,860 cases. Proration matches the documented calendar-month policy; I found no additional blockers.

Reviewed `f73b00d` against `main` at `7f89e48`. No files changed.
